page: Amazon Web Services g4ad.xlarge is a graphics-intensive instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs, corresponding to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The system is configured with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding 4.0 GB of memory per core. Graphics acceleration is provided by a single AMD Radeon Pro Navi V520 GPU with 8 GB of VRAM. Local storage is bundled as a 150 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and the instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals modest performance characteristics for the CPU and memory subsystems. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests register in the bottom 10%, and memory bandwidth read and write benchmarks fall within the bottom 25%. However, single-threaded operations show moderate capability, with gzip compression and bzip3 decompression performing in the middle 50%. Geekbench single-core scores are average, while multi-core performance, software compilation, and ray tracing benchmarks place in the bottom 25%. For language model tasks, the instance achieves an average text generation speed of 103.47 tokens per second on a small 135M model, but drops to a poor 5.34 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the g4ad.xlarge offers a specialized resource profile by bundling dedicated GPU hardware and local NVMe storage with a lighter CPU configuration. This makes it a practical option for workloads that require hardware-accelerated graphics without demanding high-end multi-core CPU performance or massive memory bandwidth. The instance is best suited for entry-level graphics-intensive applications, basic virtual workstations, light GPU-accelerated rendering, and small-scale machine learning inference tasks.
